title: Minimum of a Rotated Array

concept.title: Compare the middle with the right end
body: In a rotated sorted array of different numbers the minimum is the place where the order "restarts". Compare `a[mid]` with the last element `a[hi]`: if `a[mid] > a[hi]`, the restart is to the right of `mid`. Otherwise the part from `mid` to `hi` is sorted, so the minimum is at `mid` or to its left.
The index of the minimum is also the number of places the array was rotated to the left.

statement: A sorted array of `n` different integers was rotated at an unknown place. Print the smallest element and its index (counting from 0).
inputFormat: The second line has the rotated array.
outputFormat: Print the minimum and its index, separated by a space.
hints: If `a[mid] > a[hi]` the minimum is right of `mid`: `lo = mid + 1`.
Otherwise it is at `mid` or left of it: `hi = mid`.

explanation: If the middle is greater than the last element, the drop lies to the right; otherwise the minimum is at the middle or to its left. The range shrinks to the minimum.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

lo, hi = 0, n - 1
while lo < hi:
    mid = (lo + hi) // 2
    if a[mid] > a[hi]:
        lo = mid + 1
    else:
        hi = mid
print(a[lo], lo)
